label.webhooks.note: a community adapter's capability on the Adapters tab, in a list: webhooks · suppression pull · batch 50

label.suppressionPull.note: it pulls the provider's suppression list

label.suppressionPush.note: it pushes the shared suppression list to the provider

terms.allowed.message: The adapter's manifest says the provider's terms allow bulk marketing to opted-in lists.
terms.allowed.note: what a community adapter's provider allows, on Routing, when its manifest says nothing more

terms.forbidden: The adapter's manifest says the provider's terms forbid bulk marketing: use it for Automations and System mail.

events.webhooks.note: Sending providers › Adapters: how events come back

events.none.note: Sending providers › Adapters: no events come back

domain.api.note: Sending providers › Adapters: how a sending domain is set up

domain.manual.note: the domain's DNS records are added by hand

suppression.pull.note: Sending providers › Adapters: the suppression sync

suppression.local.note: suppressions are kept in ReputeCast only

call.endpointRefused.message: The address set for the {name} adapter is refused: {error}.
call.endpointRefused.note: a call to a community adapter failed; error: why the address is refused

call.noAddress.message: The {name} adapter has no address yet. An instance admin sets it with `reputecast adapter set-url {id} '<url>'`.
call.noAddress.note: the command between backticks is a command line: keep it as it is

call.paused.message: The {name} adapter isn't answering, so ReputeCast pauses calls to it until {until}.

call.busy.message: {count} calls to the {name} adapter were already waiting.

call.cutOff: The {name} adapter's answer was cut off: {error}.

call.invalid.message: The {name} adapter answered {op} outside the protocol: {error}.
call.invalid.note: op: the protocol operation (send); error: what was wrong with the answer

call.signature.message: The {name} adapter rejected ReputeCast's signature. Issue a new secret with `reputecast adapter secret {id}`, set it on the adapter process, and check both clocks.
call.signature.note: the command between backticks is a command line: keep it as it is

problem.manifestUnusable.note: error: what is wrong with it

problem.keyTaken.message: {other} is already registered as {key}. Update or remove it, or install the adapter under another id.
problem.keyTaken.note: other: an installed adapter's name; key: community:example-esp

problem.address.note: error: why the address is refused

problem.inUse.message: {count} connected provider(s) use {name}. Disconnect them first.

problem.adminOnly: Community adapters run for every workspace on this instance, so only instance admins can see or change where they run.
